🚀 We’re Hiring: Technical Project Manager (LATAM / Canada Only)

Are you an experienced Project Manager who thrives in a fast-paced agency environment and can own client delivery end-to-end? We’re looking for someone to manage complex e-commerce, software, and digital integration projects across mid-market and enterprise clients.

This isn’t a ticket-pusher role—we need a strategic, organized leader who understands contract scope, tracks budgets/burn rates, and can collaborate on pre-sales and proposals.

📍 Location: Remote (Open strictly to applicants located in LATAM or Canada)
⏰ Schedule: Must overlap with US Eastern Business Hours (EST)

What You’ll Do:
Client Delivery amp; Account Management: Own day-to-day delivery, run client syncs/QBRs, manage milestones/UAT/go-live, and keep clients aligned across Shopify, Magento, headless, and API integration builds.

Scope amp; Finance Control: Track SOWs, retainers, change orders, and monthly client hours. Ensure no work is treated as revenue until signed.

Pre-Sales amp; Proposals: Partner with sales to shape RFPs, turn technical estimates into milestone-driven SOWs, and lead smooth client kickoffs.

Resource Management: Coordinate internal/contract developers, architects, and QA across active projects and flag capacity early.

Processes amp; Tooling: Maintain ClickUp as the single source of truth and leverage AI tools to streamline documentation and reporting.

What You Bring:

4+ years of Project Management experience in a digital agency, e-commerce, or software environment.

Proven track record running multiple concurrent accounts (projects + retainer models).

Strong grip on SOWs, change orders, budget management, and burn rates.

Technical proficiency to comfortably manage developer conversations (Shopify, Magento, APIs, SSO) and translate technical topics for client stakeholders.

Fluent/Native-level written and verbal English with confident client-facing experience.

Hands-on experience with ClickUp (or Jira/Asana) and Microsoft 365.

Nice to Haves:

Pre-sales/RFP solutioning experience.

Technical PM or development background.

PMP, PSM, or CSM certification.

How to Apply:
📩 Interested or know someone who’s a great fit? Send your resume and portfolio/experience summary to diamante@fortiscend.com with the subject line Application: Project Manager (LATAM/Canada).

Closed mouths don’t get fed. So here goes.

I’m looking for paid work and asking my network to connect me with people who are hiring, contracting, or staffing important projects and initiatives. I’m open to full-time, contract, 1099, fractional, or project-based work. I care more about the scope of the problem and the work than the title attached to it. Meaningful work and fair compensation matter most.

And now for the harder part: I need work. 

I’m used to being the person people call to solve the problem, not the person asking for help. 

So I’m asking.

I’ve learned that I’m at my best when the work is complex, cross-functional, and needs to move from ambiguity to execution. Teams and leaders have relied on me most when:

• A critical initiative has stalled or is at risk. I bring structure, clarify ownership, align stakeholders, unblock decisions, and restore momentum.
• Strategy needs to become operating reality. I translate direction into programs, roadmaps, implementation, governance, and ways of working that teams can execute.
• Operations are not scaling with the business. I strengthen processes, roles, handoffs, and controls to improve efficiency, consistency, experience, and risk management.
• A new capability needs to be built before every answer is known. I bring structure to ambiguity and move the work from concept to implementation.
• A risk, incident, or governance issue needs resolution. I clarify accountability, drive remediation, and strengthen the oversight and lifecycle practices needed going forward.

My deepest domain experience is in employment and workforce, HR technology, enterprise products and technology, and responsible AI. I can operate at the strategy table. I can also roll up my sleeves to build, drive, and run the work. I’ve done this across enterprise technology, defense, and global development at Workday, BAE Systems, and Chemonics. 

I’ve also built commercially ready capabilities through CultureClusive in AI governance, human oversight, and accountability for high-impact or high-risk AI that can materially affect people’s opportunities, access, treatment, eligibility, safety, or outcomes. That includes the Oversight & Accountability Stress Test℠, designed to help leaders determine whether the original basis for relying on an AI system still holds as AI capabilities and operating conditions change, and surface emerging risk while management still has choices.

If someone came to mind while reading this, please make the introduction. If you can’t, DM me their name. 

You do not have to find me a job—unless you’re the one hiring. Otherwise, just help me get connected to the right person.


Thank you.

Both halves needed the same thing: knowing what is being measured, checking it, and explaining it to the people who have to use it.

Last week, a junior ServiceNow candidate came to us asking if they should abandon 𝗜𝗧𝗢𝗠 for AI.

They had two years in IT, a year on ServiceNow, and four certifications across CSA, CAD, ITSM, and ITOM. 

Despite working on capacity planning and infrastructure monitoring, they shared the same doubts we hear weekly: Is ITOM saturated? Is 𝗔𝗜 a better path? 🧭

As 𝙎𝙚𝙧𝙫𝙞𝙘𝙚𝙉𝙤𝙬 contract recruitment specialists, we rarely see true junior ITOM roles. 

Most ITOM contractors are mid-to-senior professionals with deep infrastructure backgrounds.

Here is what we are seeing across the ServiceNow contract market:

ITOM is underserved, not saturated. Everyone is chasing AI, but enterprise AI fails when the CMDB is broken. Demand for Discovery, Service Mapping, Event Management, and CSDM alignment far outweighs supply. 

Senior 𝗜𝗧𝗢𝗠 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 remain some of the hardest profiles to source. 🔍

ITOM pays well because it requires deep technical skills. It goes beyond basic Discovery configuration into OS, networking, cloud, APIs, and complex troubleshooting. This high barrier to entry limits junior roles but creates premium rates for experienced contractors.

ITOM and AI are complementary. 𝗘𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝗔𝗜 depends on accurate service models and reliable infrastructure data from ITOM. Building ITOM expertise supports AI initiatives rather than replacing them.

For early-career ServiceNow professionals: Focus on practical depth over accumulating certifications. Master OS and networking fundamentals, understand CSDM deeply, and focus on real-world troubleshooting. 

Rare technical skills drive long-term value in the 𝗦𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲𝗡𝗼𝘄 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁 ecosystem.

Last week, a junior ServiceNow candidate came to us asking if they should abandon 𝗜𝗧𝗢𝗠 for AI.

They had two years in IT, a year on ServiceNow, and four certifications across CSA, CAD, ITSM, and ITOM.

Despite working on capacity planning and infrastructure monitoring, they shared the same doubts we hear weekly: Is ITOM saturated? Is 𝗔𝗜 a better path? 🧭

As 𝙎𝙚𝙧𝙫𝙞𝙘𝙚𝙉𝙤𝙬 contract recruitment specialists, we rarely see true junior ITOM roles.

Most ITOM contractors are mid-to-senior professionals with deep infrastructure backgrounds.

Here is what we are seeing across the ServiceNow contract market:

ITOM is underserved, not saturated. Everyone is chasing AI, but enterprise AI fails when the CMDB is broken. Demand for Discovery, Service Mapping, Event Management, and CSDM alignment far outweighs supply. Senior 𝗜𝗧𝗢𝗠 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 remain some of the hardest profiles to source. 🔍

ITOM pays well because it requires deep technical skills. It goes beyond basic Discovery configuration into OS, networking, cloud, APIs, and complex troubleshooting. This high barrier to entry limits junior roles but creates premium rates for experienced contractors.

ITOM and AI are complementary. 𝗘𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝗔𝗜 depends on accurate service models and reliable infrastructure data from ITOM. Building ITOM expertise supports AI initiatives rather than replacing them.

For early-career ServiceNow professionals: Focus on practical depth over accumulating certifications. Master OS and networking fundamentals, understand CSDM deeply, and focus on real-world troubleshooting. Rare technical skills drive long-term value in the 𝗦𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲𝗡𝗼𝘄 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁 ecosystem.
